record.paper_title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics
record.context_brief: DHGHY sum rule and J=1 fixed poles
record.original_question: Test whether the Gerasimov-Drell-Hearn-Hosada-Yamamoto sum rule is valid in QCD, or whether it can fail because the dispersion relation for the forward spin-flip Compton amplitude contains a nonzero constant term c0, historically called a J=1 fixed pole. The open question is whether J=1 fixed poles occur in QCD bound states; their presence could spoil the sum rule even when the relevant integral converges.

evidence.quote: The question I would like to raise here is “What does the DHGHY Sum Rule test?”.
So the question of the validity of the DHGHY Sum Rule comes down to whether J = 1 fixed poles occur in QCD.
Still, the verdict is out in QCD, where bound states are not so simple.

artifact.category_tag: GDH sum rule and fixed poles in QCD
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the forward spin-flip Compton scattering amplitude on a hadronic bound-state target of mass M and anomalous magnetic moment κ in a relativistic quantum field theory. Write a once-subtracted dispersion relation in the photon energy ν for the spin-dependent forward Compton amplitude, of the form

  S(ν) = c0 + (2ν/π) ∫_{ν_th}^{∞} dν' [σ_{1/2}(ν') − σ_{3/2}(ν')] / (ν'^2 − ν^2),

where σ_{1/2} and σ_{3/2} are the total photoabsorption cross sections for parallel and antiparallel photon-target helicities, and c0 is the subtraction constant (the residue of the so-called J = 1 fixed pole in the complex angular momentum plane of the amplitude). The Gerasimov–Drell–Hearn–Hosada–Yamamoto (GDH/DHGHY) sum rule

  ∫_{ν_th}^{∞} [σ_{1/2}(ν) − σ_{3/2}(ν)] (dν/ν) = −2π^2 α κ^2 / M^2

is obtained under the assumption c0 = 0 and convergence of the low-energy expansion.

Problem. Determine, within QCD as the theory of strong interactions for hadronic bound states (e.g., the proton), whether the subtraction constant c0 in the forward spin-flip Compton dispersion relation is necessarily zero, or whether a nonzero J = 1 fixed-pole contribution can arise from the bound-state structure. Equivalently, decide whether the GDH/DHGHY sum rule is an exact consequence of QCD for hadronic bound states, or whether it can be modified by an additive c0 ≠ 0 term even when the dispersive integral converges.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up no definitive proof or disproof concerning the existence of J = 1 fixed poles in the forward spin-flip Compton amplitude for hadronic bound states in QCD. Experimental tests of the GDH sum rule on the proton are consistent with it at roughly the 10% level, and generalized GDH sum rules have been studied with radiative and power QCD corrections, but a rigorous resolution of whether QCD bound-state dynamics produce a nonzero c0 subtraction constant does not appear in the available literature. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: QCD radiative and power corrections and Generalized GDH sum rules
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized GDH sum rules studied with QCD radiative and power corrections; GDH integral sensitive to QCD power corrections.
status_evidence.claim: Active theoretical study of GDH-type sum rules in QCD continues, without a definitive verdict on the fixed-pole contribution.

status_evidence.title: Sum rules (quantum field theory) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: GDH sum rule assumes causality, unitarity, Lorentz/gauge invariance; experimentally verified within ~10%.
status_evidence.claim: Status of GDH sum rule in QCD remains a test rather than a derived theorem from bound-state QCD.

status_evidence.title: New sum rules from low energy Compton scattering on arbitrary spin target
status_evidence.snippet: Low-energy Compton sum rules extended; subtraction-function issues remain a subject of ongoing investigation.
status_evidence.claim: The role of subtraction constants/fixed poles in Compton dispersion relations remains under active investigation.
